attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in a co-signed op-ed he endorsed. The Politico quote that follows is separate, but the causal claim itself is his.

semantics.note: Faithful to the sentence: state regulatory momentum is a specific reason Big Tech wants federal preemption. 'Shut the states down' is rhetoric, fairly read as restricting state AI rules.

contract.note: Plain reading is ordinary. It does not require the motive to be exclusive and relies on reasons the companies stated themselves, not private intent. That is a fair test for a claim about why companies lobby.

evidence.note: OpenAI's March 2025 submission, before the post, asks for relief from 781+ proposed state AI bills and calls the patchwork a reason for preemption. Company disclosure of its stated rationale.
Google's March 2025 submission, before the post, asks for federal preemption of state frontier-AI laws to avoid a fragmented patchwork. Company disclosure of its stated rationale.

reviews.rationale: Two major firms' submissions, made before the post, explicitly tie their preemption requests to proliferating state AI rules. That meets the support condition. Limits: these show stated reasons, not private motives, and cover two firms, not all of Big Tech. The packet has no counterevidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in an op-ed he co-signed and endorsed.

semantics.note: 'Would only invite' is firm, unhedged conditional language. The antecedent (absence of oversight) is kept. The separate claim about past self-regulation is correctly left out.

contract.note: Reading the antecedent as removal of state oversight with no federal replacement fits the post. Read instead as 'no federal law', the antecedent might already hold, so the reading decides whether the claim is scored. No baseline or deadline is imposed.

evidence.note: Law-firm alert dated Oct 1, 2026: no federal preemption has been enacted and state AI laws remain in effect. This shows the antecedent did not occur; it is not evidence of the outcome.
GMU tracker dated Oct 21, 2026: state AI law is still in force, with only narrow injunctions. This shows the antecedent is unmet; it is not evidence about lobbying.

December 2025 White House executive order directing challenges to state AI laws. It is a government record, mislabelled as a company disclosure. It shows an effort to remove state oversight, not that oversight was removed.

reviews.rationale: Conditional forecast with no deadline. Evidence up to Oct 2026 shows state oversight was not broadly removed, so the antecedent has not occurred and the forecast cannot be scored. There is no before-and-after lobbying evidence tied to such a gap, and the antecedent could still happen later.
